title: Introduce windowed prefetch orchestrator and occupancy spectrogram exporter
author: Sofia Liang
description:
Motivation: Production workloads at Redwood show recurring micro-bursts where KV-cache priming and early-token contention drive p95 tails. Existing prefetch heuristics operate at request granularity and either overfetch (wasting cycles) or underfetch (leaving kernels starved). This PR introduces a windowed prefetch orchestrator that reasons about short-term sequence arrival patterns and issues targeted prefetches for likely-following token prefixes, coupled with a lightweight telemetry exporter that emits a time-windowed "occupancy spectrogram" (token occupancy vs. time) for downstream analysis.

Design summary: The orchestrator observes recent request headers (sequence length, context similarity fingerprint, and token delta frequency) in a sliding window (default 250ms) and schedules prefetch jobs with an affinity score to GPU execution lanes. Prefetches are bounded by a per-model token budget and cancelable on eviction pressure. The occupancy spectrogram exporter aggregates per-core occupancy over 50ms bins and encodes a compact spectrogram with quantized occupancy buckets and a sparse run-length encoding to keep telemetry size low.

Implementation notes: - New package bench/prefetch_orchestrator: contains the sliding-window sampler, affinity scorer, budget manager, and a small runtime shim that plugs into the existing batcher dispatch hooks. - New package bench/telemetry/occupancy_exporter: emits OTLP-compatible traces/metrics and a compact spectrogram protobuf (bench.proto) for offline histogram reconstruction. - Integration with the existing bench harness is gated by a feature flag (--enable-windowed-prefetch) and controlled by a new config block under bench.workload.<model>.prefetch.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc referenced in the PR (link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-9876/windowed-prefetch-design) - [x] Unit tests for affinity scorer and budget manager - [x] Integration test against the mixed-seq runner - [x] Perf harness runs and baseline comparison attached - [x] Telemetry schema added and registered

Testing and results: Ran mixed-sequence benchmark (session-mix-v2) on a 4xA100 testbed with the following observations compared to the baseline (no windowed prefetch): - Aggregate token throughput +6.8% (median across 10 runs) - p95 latency reduced by 11.7% under synthetic bursty load (burst ratio 3x) - Memory overhead increased by ~3.9% due to short-lived prefetch buffers - On steady low-concurrency workloads there was <1% difference in cost, indicating the orchestrator backs off correctly.

Operational considerations: - Default budgets are conservative. We recommend a staged rollout: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with telemetry-driven knobs. - The spectrogram exporter is opt-in; when enabled it emits a compact artifact per epoch and a sample manifest for correlating with kernel flamegraphs.

Follow-ups: - Add an adaptive budget resizer that ties budget to observed hit-rate. - Expose an HTTP live-inspector for the spectrogram artifacts (separate PR).

review_conversation:
Alex Murphy: Nice clean split between sampler and scorer. Two asks: (1) we should have an explicit eviction metric when budget cancels prefetches so SRE can tune; (2) add a safety net to never prefetch past sequence max_token_limit.

Sofia Liang (author): Reply: added eviction counter and exposed it via the exporter; also added saturation check against model max_token_limit earlier in the pipeline (see budget_manager.go).

Rajat Singh: Observed a flake in the integration test on CI where the sampler window time drifted causing races under heavy concurrency. Suggest using a mocked time source in unit tests for deterministic runs.

Sofia Liang: Switched tests to use bench/testclock and tightened synchronization; pushed a follow-up commit.

Camille Ortega: Approved after verifying the perf artifacts and telemetry sizes. Left a comment to include a short blurb in the deployment runbook about spectrogram artifact retention.

Alex Murphy: Squash-merged after resolving comments.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash by Alex Murphy on 2026-02-20. Merge method: squash and merge. Commit message preserved: "bench: add windowed prefetch orchestrator and occupancy spectrogram exporter"
release_notes: Introduces an opt-in windowed prefetch orchestrator to reduce p95 latency in bursty workloads and a compact occupancy spectrogram exporter for telemetry-driven tuning. Opt-in and conservative defaults; no breaking changes.
